Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 19 binds us as well as the vendor, and it is a no-hire ("agree not to hire ... any employee of the other party"), not a non-solicit. It also reaches all employees of the other party, not just personnel involved in the services, extends to affiliates, and has no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions and restrictions covering all vendor personnel are walk-away items under the rule, so this fails the fallback on material terms notwithstanding the acceptable 12-month tail. Because the mutual structure is already part of the bargain, we narrowed to the fallback rather than deleting the clause outright: mutual solicitation-only restriction, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

Original paragraphs:
p0133: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0133: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of the relevant individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement, neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement. This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person, and does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis or in response to such general advertisement.

Comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all employees, so we have narrowed this to a mutual non-solicitation of personnel directly involved in the services for twelve months after their involvement ends, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. This reflects our playbook fallback position on restrictive covenants.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Sparkling:

- **§ 2 (Grant)** — the licence is "non-transferable and non-exclusive," a limit on Garman's grant, not a restriction on our sourcing.
- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — ordinary licence-scope limits (no copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing, use outside authorisation); no requirements-purchase or "shall not procure from any third party" covenant.
- **§ 10 / § 11 (Maintenance and Fees)** — maintenance is a renewable one-year service commitment from Garman; it does not appoint Garman as our sole or exclusive provider.
- Other "exclusive" hits are the § 15 exclusive-remedy clause, the § 16 non-exclusive escrow licence, and non-exclusive jurisdiction in the governing-law provision — none is a restrictive covenant on us.

This sits at the playbook's preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer), so we keep full freedom to buy from other suppliers and no change is needed.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sparkling. The only uses of "exclusive" are the non-exclusive licence grants (§ 2 and the escrow licence in § 16), the exclusive-remedy provision in § 15 and the non-exclusive jurisdiction clause — none restricts our freedom to source software, maintenance or related services elsewhere. The restrictions in § 3 are ordinary licence-scope limits (no copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing) and contain no requirements-purchase or "shall not procure from any third party" covenant, and § 10 maintenance/§ 11 fees do not make Garman our sole provider. Searches for "sole", "requirements from", "competing" and "third party" returned nothing of that character. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer), so no redline is required.

This meets the fallback position, so classifying it as compliant and not redlining is correct under the playbook's classification semantics.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact — the indemnity is framed as breach of the IP ownership/non-infringement warranty rather than using the words 'infringe or misappropriate' — and does not undermine the substantive conclusion.

There is no reciprocal or one-way Customer indemnity anywhere, and Section 15 expressly carves Section 13 out of the damages limitation, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap and clearly not walk-away territory; flagging would be over-flagging.

Shortfalls versus preferred (no express duty to defend/control the defence, no refund remedy, no extension to breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and a tight ten-day notice period) are correctly recorded in the rationale as noted-but-not-flagged sub-elements rather than raised as deviations.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 15 is the only liability provision in the agreement (Sections 12 and 13 contain no cap language, and there is no "aggregate liability" wording elsewhere). It is mutual and mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, and it carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap at all — direct damages are open-ended for both parties, including for Sparkling. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of twelve months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirmed that Sparkling's fee payment obligations are not capped damages, retaining the existing Section 13/14 carve-out. Note that "fees" is not a defined term but is set by the Fee Schedule (Section 11), so the cap basis is the full licence and maintenance fee stream rather than an illusory set-up fee.

Original paragraphs:
p0105: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0105: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights; and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this cap. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties' direct liability is open-ended; we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement remain outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages; a straight twelve months' fees cap is our fallback.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling:

- **§3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the only section binding us with prohibitions — is confined to ordinary licence hygiene: no copying beyond backups, no transfer/sublicence, no reverse engineering, and "not use the Work except as authorized herein." Nothing touches what businesses we run or what products we buy or build.
- **§2 (Grant of License)** is a non-exclusive licence with no exclusivity, minimum-purchase, or sole-source commitment on us.
- **§14 (Confidentiality)** expressly carves out independently developed information (p0098), so it does not operate as a back-door restraint on internal development.
- **§19** is a mutual, one-year employee non-solicit — a different category, reciprocal, and not a restriction on our business lines.
- Text sweeps for "compet", "similar", "exclusive", and "shall not develop/market/sell/engage/acquire/distribute" surfaced no restrictive covenant binding us (the only "compet" hit was "competence" in §9).

This sits at the rule's **preferred** position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so nothing to negotiate here.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) is limited to conventional software-licence protections (no copying beyond backup, no sublicence/transfer, no reverse engineering, use only as authorized) and does not restrict the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. Section 2 grants a non-exclusive licence with no exclusivity or minimum-purchase commitment on us; Section 14 (Confidentiality) preserves an independent-development carve-out (p0098) rather than a residual-use restraint; and Section 19 is a mutual employee non-solicit (a separate category, and reciprocal). Sweeps for "compet", "similar", "exclusive" and "shall not develop/market/sell/engage" returned no restrictive covenant binding us. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is required.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic in either direction. Pricing provisions (Section 11 Fees, Section 10 maintenance fees, Section 2 additional-location fees, Section 17 perpetuity conditioned on fee payment) simply refer to the Fee Schedule; searches for "most favoured/favourable", "best price", "other customers", "competitor" and price/rate matching language returned nothing, and the general provisions (Section 20) contain no such covenant. Sparkling therefore has no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which is the playbook's preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer). Nothing to redline; we would of course welcome a Garman-granted MFN in our favour if it can be negotiated.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

reasons: The cited Section 15 contains only an exclusive-remedy/consequential-damages exclusion and a Sections 13/14 carve-out — there is no monetary cap, so it fails the fallback's requirement of a mutual cap of twelve months' fees (and leaves Customer's direct liability open-ended), making the deviation classification correct rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The redline edits the existing paragraph rather than rewriting the section: it inserts the model mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), the Excluded Claims carve-out set (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and the payment-obligations-are-not-damages clarification, while preserving the pre-existing Section 13/14 carve-out and the mutual indirect-damages exclusion.

Directionality is correct for the Customer side: the cap is mutual and the fee basis is the licence/maintenance fee stream (not an illusory set-up fee), and no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic is explained by the necessary insertion of two substantive sentences into a short paragraph; the underlying original wording is left intact, so the edit is still the smallest that reaches the playbook position.
The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the playbook position and offers the straight 12-months'-fees fallback.

Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic in either direction. Pricing provisions (Section 11 Fees, Section 10 maintenance fees, Section 2 additional-location fees, Section 17 perpetuity conditioned on fee payment) simply refer to the Fee Schedule; searches for "most favoured/favourable", "best price", "other customers", "competitor" and price/rate matching language returned nothing, and the general provisions (Section 20) contain no such covenant. Sparkling therefore has no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which is the playbook's preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer). Nothing to redline; we would of course welcome a Garman-granted MFN in our favour if it can be negotiated.

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

paragraphs.text: 2. GRANT OF LICENSE

Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
4. DELIVERY, INSTALLATION AND DATA CONVERSION

(a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.

(b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.
13. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY

Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
1. DEFINITIONS AND SCHEDULES
In this Agreement the following definitions shall apply:
(a) Authorized Locations means the locations listed in Schedule "C."
(b) Confidential Information has the meaning specified in Section 14.
(c) Documentation means the documentation related to use of the Software described in Schedule "B."
(d) Maintenance Commencement Date means the date that acceptance testing is successfully completed at all of the Authorized Locations.
(e) Maintenance Services means the Software Update Service, Telephone Support Service and Software Repair Service described in Section 10.
(f) Modifications means the modifications set out in Schedule "D."

(g) Person includes an individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, unincorporated organization, the Crown or any agency or instrumentality thereof or any other judicial entity recognized by law.
(h) Software means the software described in Schedule "B."
(i) Specifications means the specifications set out in Schedule "D."
(j) Work means the Software and the Documentation collectively.
The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement:

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us an unconditional convenience termination right at any time on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge anywhere in the Agreement (no non-refundability or termination-fee language appears in the fee provisions). Garman has no convenience right: its only termination triggers are the insolvency events and uncured material default in Section 17(c), and the maintenance term in Section 10 simply runs as a renewable one-year term. The 90-day notice period sits at the fallback rather than our preferred 30 days, and the Agreement is silent on a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (Section 17(c) provides a return of fees for services not rendered only on termination for Garman's default) — both are minor sub-elements short of the preferred position and not worth a redline given the otherwise clean, penalty-free exit and the perpetual (non-committed-term) licence structure.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us an unconditional convenience termination right at any time on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge anywhere in the Agreement (no non-refundability or termination-fee language appears in the fee provisions). Garman has no convenience right: its only termination triggers are the insolvency events and uncured material default in Section 17(c), and the maintenance term in Section 10 simply runs as a renewable one-year term. The 90-day notice period sits at the fallback rather than our preferred 30 days, and the Agreement is silent on a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (Section 17(c) provides a return of fees for services not rendered only on termination for Garman's default) — both are minor sub-elements short of the preferred position and not worth a redline given the otherwise clean, penalty-free exit and the perpetual (non-committed-term) licence structure.

paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;

(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

paragraphs.text: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
Sparkling shall:
(a) not copy the Software except to copy it onto another AS400 at the Authorized Locations and to make copies of the Software at each Authorized Location solely for backup purposes;
(b) not copy any of the Documentation except as required for Sparkling's internal purposes related to Sparkling's use of the Software;
(c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
(d) not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the Software;
(e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
(f) take all reasonable precautions to prevent third parties from using

the Work in any way that would constitute a breach of this Agreement including, without limitation, such precautions as Sparkling would otherwise take to protect its own proprietary software or hardware or information; and
1. DEFINITIONS AND SCHEDULES
In this Agreement the following definitions shall apply:
(a) Authorized Locations means the locations listed in Schedule "C."
(b) Confidential Information has the meaning specified in Section 14.
(c) Documentation means the documentation related to use of the Software described in Schedule "B."
(d) Maintenance Commencement Date means the date that acceptance testing is successfully completed at all of the Authorized Locations.
(e) Maintenance Services means the Software Update Service, Telephone Support Service and Software Repair Service described in Section 10.
(f) Modifications means the modifications set out in Schedule "D."

(g) Person includes an individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, unincorporated organization, the Crown or any agency or instrumentality thereof or any other judicial entity recognized by law.
(h) Software means the software described in Schedule "B."
(i) Specifications means the specifications set out in Schedule "D."
(j) Work means the Software and the Documentation collectively.
The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement:

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Planner hints:

**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience.

- **Our exit right:** § 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the Agreement. That meets the fallback (60–90 days' notice, no fee above 3 months' fees).

No redline proposed.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 17(b) gives us an unconditional convenience termination right at any time on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge anywhere in the Agreement (no non-refundability or termination-fee language appears in the fee provisions). Garman has no convenience right: its only termination triggers are the insolvency events and uncured material default in Section 17(c), and the maintenance term in Section 10 simply runs as a renewable one-year term. The 90-day notice period sits at the fallback rather than our preferred 30 days, and the Agreement is silent on a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (Section 17(c) provides a return of fees for services not rendered only on termination for Garman's default) — both are minor sub-elements short of the preferred position and not worth a redline given the otherwise clean, penalty-free exit and the perpetual (non-committed-term) licence structure.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (§10, p0065) with no automatic renewal language anywhere in the Agreement — renewal therefore requires the parties' agreement, which matches the preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement, 12-month periods). There is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no multi-year auto-renewal, so no walk-away or fallback issue arises; exit is further protected because the licence is perpetual while fees are paid and Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice (§17(a)-(b)). Note only as a sub-element: the Fee Schedule mechanics (§11) contain no cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal (preferred is the lesser of CPI and 3%); consistent with the playbook, a missing price-uplift cap is noted rather than flagged, and we can raise it commercially if the Fee Schedule permits unilateral increases.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (§10, p0065) with no automatic renewal language anywhere in the Agreement — renewal therefore requires the parties' agreement, which matches the preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement, 12-month periods). There is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no multi-year auto-renewal, so no walk-away or fallback issue arises; exit is further protected because the licence is perpetual while fees are paid and Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice (§17(a)-(b)). Note only as a sub-element: the Fee Schedule mechanics (§11) contain no cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal (preferred is the lesser of CPI and 3%); consistent with the playbook, a missing price-uplift cap is noted rather than flagged, and we can raise it commercially if the Fee Schedule permits unilateral increases.

paragraphs.text: 17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

(a) Time shall be of the essence with respect to all matters under this Agreement.

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (§10, p0065) with no automatic renewal language anywhere in the Agreement — renewal therefore requires the parties' agreement, which matches the preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement, 12-month periods). There is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no multi-year auto-renewal, so no walk-away or fallback issue arises; exit is further protected because the licence is perpetual while fees are paid and Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice (§17(a)-(b)). Note only as a sub-element: the Fee Schedule mechanics (§11) contain no cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal (preferred is the lesser of CPI and 3%); consistent with the playbook, a missing price-uplift cap is noted rather than flagged, and we can raise it commercially if the Fee Schedule permits unilateral increases.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Planner hints:

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only governing-law/venue provision (§20(h), p0146) selects Nova Scotia and Canadian law with the courts of Nova Scotia — the vendor's home jurisdiction and outside the accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales. It therefore fails both the preferred and the fallback position on a material term. The venue is non-exclusive rather than an exclusive foreign forum, so this stops short of walk-away territory, but the choice of law still requires correction. No arbitration clause exists elsewhere in the document. We propose the smallest edit to the preferred position (New York law; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County), keeping the sentence structure intact, and flag Delaware, California, or England and Wales as acceptable fallbacks.

Original paragraphs:
p0146: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0146: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

Comment:
[Playbook] We moved governing law and venue to our accepted New York position, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County. Nova Scotia is outside our accepted list; if helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (courts of London) as a fallback.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) is a blanket bar on assignment by either party absent the other's written consent, with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard on consent; Section 3(c) reinforces this one-sidedly against Sparkling (and the licence itself is "non-transferable" under Section 2). That fails even the fallback (successor assignment on written notice, consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in walk-away territory for a customer M&A event. Termination triggers in Section 17 contain no change-of-control right for Garman, which is acceptable; the redline preserves that by stating expressly that our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right, and adds the affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonableness standard and no-competitor limit on Garman assignments.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling and a reasonableness standard on Garman assignments
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added customary affiliate and transaction successor rights so an internal reorganisation or M&A deal does not require Garman's consent, and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard with no assignment to our competitors. We also conformed Section 3(c) to this carve-out.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Sparkling may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Garman to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates, upon written notice to Garman. Garman may not assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Sparkling, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Sparkling. Except as set out above, neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. No change of control of Sparkling shall give Garman any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

ops.oldText: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer
ops.newText: (c) except as permitted by Section 20(d), not assign this Agreement or transfer
