Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) is a blanket bar on assignment by either party absent the other's written consent, with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard on consent; Section 3(c) reinforces this one-sidedly against Sparkling (and the licence itself is "non-transferable" under Section 2). That fails even the fallback (successor assignment on written notice, consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in walk-away territory for a customer M&A event. Termination triggers in Section 17 contain no change-of-control right for Garman, which is acceptable; the redline preserves that by stating expressly that our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right, and adds the affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonableness standard and no-competitor limit on Garman assignments.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

- **Issue:** Section 20(d) (p0142) imposes a flat mutual bar on assignment without the other party's written consent — no affiliate carve-out, no M&A/successor carve-out, and no "not unreasonably withheld" standard. Section 3(c) (p0033) compounds this one-sidedly, barring Sparkling from assigning except as authorised by Garman in writing, and Section 2 grants only a "non-transferable" licence. This fails the fallback position (successor assignment on written notice with a reasonableness standard) and would block a Sparkling reorganisation or sale.
- **Good news:** Section 17's termination triggers contain no change-of-control right for Garman, and no re-pricing trigger exists anywhere in the document.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganisation or sale of substantially all assets on written notice; Garman may assign only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Sparkling competitor; residual consents subject to a reasonableness standard; express confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) conformed with an "except as permitted by Section 20(d)" opener.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 20(d) is a blanket bar on assignment by either party absent the other's written consent, with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard on consent; Section 3(c) reinforces this one-sidedly against Sparkling (and the licence itself is "non-transferable" under Section 2). That fails even the fallback (successor assignment on written notice, consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in walk-away territory for a customer M&A event. Termination triggers in Section 17 contain no change-of-control right for Garman, which is acceptable; the redline preserves that by stating expressly that our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right, and adds the affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonableness standard and no-competitor limit on Garman assignments.

Original paragraphs:
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0142: (d) Sparkling may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Garman to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates, upon written notice to Garman. Garman may not assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Sparkling, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Sparkling. Except as set out above, neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. No change of control of Sparkling shall give Garman any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
p0033: (c) except as permitted by Section 20(d), not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;

Comment:
[Playbook] We added customary affiliate and transaction successor rights so an internal reorganisation or M&A deal does not require Garman's consent, and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard with no assignment to our competitors. We also conformed Section 3(c) to this carve-out.

input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 vests ownership of the whole Work in Garman, expressly including the "Modifications" set out in Schedule "D" — i.e. the bespoke work we commission and pay for — and states that no title passes to us. The only counterbalance is the narrow Section 2 licence to use the Software and Documentation at Authorized Locations, which does not on its face extend to Improvements or Modifications and carries no modify/sublicence rights (Section 3(c)-(d)). The Agreement is also silent on ownership of our data: Section 4(b) has Garman converting "Sparkling's data" and Section 14 treats it only as mutual Confidential Information, with no statement that we retain all rights in it. That falls short of both the preferred position (we own what is created for us; Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is licensed back perpetually) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables), so it is a material deviation on a critical rule. We have not disturbed Garman's ownership of its underlying software, which the playbook accepts; the minimal edit adds a carve-out confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP and that our (already perpetual, per Section 17(a)) licence covers Improvements and Modifications.

proposal.summary: Add Sparkling data/IP ownership carve-out to Section 13 and confirm the Section 2 licence extends to Improvements and Modifications
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives Garman ownership of the Work including the Modifications we fund, and the Agreement says nothing about our own data, so we have added a short carve-out confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP and that our licence extends to Improvements and Modifications. Our playbook requires that we keep ownership of Customer Data and receive a perpetual, royalty-free licence to anything created for us; we are content for Garman to retain ownership of its underlying software.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to its data (including data converted pursuant to Section 4) and its pre-existing intellectual property, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Garman any ownership of, or licence to use (other than as necessary to perform Garman's obligations hereunder), Sparkling's data or intellectual property. The licence granted in Section 2 extends to all Improvements and Modifications and, subject to Section 17(a), is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free.

input.rationale: Section 13 vests ownership of the whole Work in Garman, expressly including the "Modifications" set out in Schedule "D" — i.e. the bespoke work we commission and pay for — and states that no title passes to us. The only counterbalance is the narrow Section 2 licence to use the Software and Documentation at Authorized Locations, which does not on its face extend to Improvements or Modifications and carries no modify/sublicence rights (Section 3(c)-(d)). The Agreement is also silent on ownership of our data: Section 4(b) has Garman converting "Sparkling's data" and Section 14 treats it only as mutual Confidential Information, with no statement that we retain all rights in it. That falls short of both the preferred position (we own what is created for us; Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is licensed back perpetually) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables), so it is a material deviation on a critical rule. We have not disturbed Garman's ownership of its underlying software, which the playbook accepts; the minimal edit adds a carve-out confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP and that our (already perpetual, per Section 17(a)) licence covers Improvements and Modifications.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

reasons: The cited clause (s.20(d)) is a flat mutual consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, so it fails the fallback (successor assignment on notice; consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in the rule's walk-away zone for a Customer M&A event — 'deviation' is the correct classification.

The redline implements the preferred position directionally in our favour: unilateral Customer right to assign to affiliates/successors on notice, Vendor assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, residual mutual consent softened by a reasonableness standard, and an express no-termination/no-re-pricing statement on Customer change of control, per the redline guidance.
The conforming edit to s.3(c) ('except as permitted by Section 20(d)') is necessary because that covenant otherwise re-imposes the bar on Customer assignment; it is narrowly drawn.

The failed 'minimal edit p0142' check (ratio 0.815) is acceptable here: the original single sentence had to be restructured into asymmetric assignment rights, which cannot be achieved by insertion alone.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice, though it does not expressly mention the added change-of-control sentence; the rationale correctly notes Section 17 contains no Vendor change-of-control trigger, so that sentence is confirmatory rather than a duplicate flag — a minor drafting-scope point, not a defect.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Kind: missing

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 15. LIMITATION OF GARMAN'S LIABILITY

The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:

Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. **Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§13 (p0088)** vests ownership of all IP in the "Work" in Garman, expressly including "Improvements or Modifications thereto", and confirms no title passes to us. "Modifications" is defined (§1(n)/p0014) as the modifications in Schedule "D" — the bespoke work we commission and pay for.
- The only licence back is **§2 (p0028)**: a non-transferable, non-exclusive licence to use the *Software* and *Documentation* at Authorized Locations — it does not on its face reach Improvements/Modifications, and §3(c)–(d) bar sublicensing and reverse engineering. §17(a) does at least make the licence perpetual while fees are paid, which mitigates part of the gap.
- **No Customer Data ownership statement anywhere.** §4(b) has Garman converting "Sparkling's data" and §14 treats it only as mutual Confidential Information — confidentiality is not a rights-retention statement.

Why deviation rather than compliant: Garman retaining its platform IP is acceptable, but vendor ownership of customer-funded deliverables without a clear perpetual, modify/sublicence-capable licence back, combined with silence on our data, fails both the preferred and the fallback position on material terms.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): a single inserted sentence pair after §13 confirming (i) we retain all right, title and interest in our data and pre-existing IP, with no assignment to Garman, and (ii) the §2 licence extends to Improvements and Modifications on a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free basis subject to §17(a). Garman's ownership of its underlying software is left untouched.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 13 vests ownership of the whole Work in Garman, expressly including the "Modifications" set out in Schedule "D" — i.e. the bespoke work we commission and pay for — and states that no title passes to us. The only counterbalance is the narrow Section 2 licence to use the Software and Documentation at Authorized Locations, which does not on its face extend to Improvements or Modifications and carries no modify/sublicence rights (Section 3(c)-(d)). The Agreement is also silent on ownership of our data: Section 4(b) has Garman converting "Sparkling's data" and Section 14 treats it only as mutual Confidential Information, with no statement that we retain all rights in it. That falls short of both the preferred position (we own what is created for us; Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is licensed back perpetually) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables), so it is a material deviation on a critical rule. We have not disturbed Garman's ownership of its underlying software, which the playbook accepts; the minimal edit adds a carve-out confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP and that our (already perpetual, per Section 17(a)) licence covers Improvements and Modifications.

Original paragraphs:
p0088: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
p0042: (b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0088: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to its data (including data converted pursuant to Section 4) and its pre-existing intellectual property, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Garman any ownership of, or licence to use (other than as necessary to perform Garman's obligations hereunder), Sparkling's data or intellectual property. The licence granted in Section 2 extends to all Improvements and Modifications and, subject to Section 17(a), is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 13 gives Garman ownership of the Work including the Modifications we fund, and the Agreement says nothing about our own data, so we have added a short carve-out confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP and that our licence extends to Improvements and Modifications. Our playbook requires that we keep ownership of Customer Data and receive a perpetual, royalty-free licence to anything created for us; we are content for Garman to retain ownership of its underlying software.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

reasons: Classification is correct: Section 13 vests ownership of the whole Work — expressly including the Modifications Sparkling commissions under Schedule 'D' — in Garman with no title passing to us, and the only licence (Section 2) is a non-transferable, non-exclusive right to use Software/Documentation at Authorized Locations, with no modify/sublicence rights and no express coverage of Improvements or Modifications. That fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables), so this is a genuine deviation, not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

The Customer Data gap is real and material: Section 4(b) only describes conversion of 'Sparkling's data' and Section 14 treats it as mutual Confidential Information; there is no statement that we retain all rights in our data, as the rule requires.

The redline is directionally correct and minimal: it leaves Garman's ownership of its underlying software intact (which the playbook accepts), adds the required Customer Data / pre-existing IP retention sentence, and extends the Section 2 licence to Improvements and Modifications on a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free basis. Deterministic checks confirm no assignment of Customer data/IP to the Vendor remains.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position (Customer Data ownership plus perpetual royalty-free licence), concedes Vendor platform ownership, and matches tone requirements.

Minor gaps worth noting but not disqualifying: the added licence language does not expressly add 'modify and sublicense' or worldwide scope, so the clause still sits below the stated fallback wording; and 'subject to Section 17(a), is perpetual, irrevocable' risks reading as subordinating perpetuity to termination — consider tightening both if negotiating capital allows.

(c) SOFTWARE REPAIR SERVICE

Should the Software not operate substantially in conformance with the Sparkling's Specifications in all material respects, Garman will use its best efforts to repair the Software under the support agreement at no additional charge to Sparkling. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Garman may charge a fee at its rates set out in the Fee Schedule to provide Software Repair Services which are required due to:
(1) failure due to Sparkling operator errors;

(2) failure to maintain Software at such updated version or release of the Software provided by Garman to Sparkling, from time to time, at no additional charge as part of the Maintenance Services or otherwise;
(3) material modification of the Software by Sparkling; or
(4) the Software being transferred to a different networking environment or hardware configuration without the prior written consent of Garman; or
(5) any failure of the hardware or the operating system not caused by Garman or the Software.
8. OPTION TO REJECT EXERCISED

If Sparkling exercises its option to reject the Software in accordance with Section 7, then the parties shall forthwith carry out the following actions and this Agreement will terminate upon their completion:
(a) Sparkling shall return all copies of the Work and all of Garman's Confidential Information in its possession or control to Garman.
(b) Garman shall return to Sparkling any and all amounts paid to Garman hereunder, and all of Sparkling's Confidential Information in its possession or
control.
7. OPTION TO REJECT SOFTWARE

If during the acceptance period described in Section 6, the Software has failed to perform in accordance with the Specifications and Garman has been unable to correct the deficiency within 45 business days of written notice being provided to Garman of such failure then Sparkling shall have the option, exercisable on 15 business days written notice to Garman, in lieu of any other remedy, to reject the Software. Such option shall terminate if in the interim, the Software successfully completes acceptance testing and meets the Specifications.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
input.rationale: The grant is not revocable at Garman's discretion (Section 17(a) makes it perpetual while fees are paid, terminable only for insolvency or uncured material default under Section 17(c)(7)), and affiliates are already covered without a notice condition — so the clause is above walk-away and meets the affiliate limb of the preferred position. However, it fails the fallback on transferability: the licence is expressly "non-transferable", Section 3(c) bars assignment or transfer without Garman's written consent, and Section 20(d) repeats that bar with no carve-out for a successor in an M&A transaction. Contractors acting on our behalf are also not covered (and Section 3(f)/3(e) restrict third-party use). We therefore propose a minimal edit to Section 2 adding contractors and a successor-transfer right overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d).

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf and permit transfer of the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the grant to contractors acting on our behalf and added a successor-transfer right, since our playbook requires the licence to survive a merger or sale and to cover the third parties who operate the system for us. We are happy to keep the transfer limited to a genuine M&A successor that assumes our obligations.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Planner hints:

paragraphs.text: 20. GENERAL MATTERS
(a) Time shall be of the essence with respect to all matters under this Agreement.

(b) All notices required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be given in writing and may be sent by personal delivery or facsimile transmission addressed to the recipient at the addresses shown below (or such other address as may be designated by notice in accordance with this Agreement):
PAGE 10
Garman: GARMAN ROUTING SYSTEMS, INC #1 - 502 45th Street West Saskatoon, SK S7L 6H2
Sparkling: SPARKLING SPRING WATER GROUP LIMITED 19 Fielding Avenue Dartmouth, NS B3B 1C9

Any notice sent by personal delivery shall be deemed to be given on the day of its delivery provided it is received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day. Any notices sent by facsimile transmission shall be deemed to be given on the day of transmission if received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day.

(c) Unless otherwise permitted by this Agreement, no waiver of any part of this Agreement shall be binding unless executed in writing by both parties. No waiver of any part of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other part or a continuing waiver unless otherwise agreed to in writing by both parties.
(d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

(e) The parties are acting as independent contractors under this Agreement and not as agents or representatives of the other and not as partners or joint ventures. Neither party shall enter into any agreement or commitment on behalf of the other without the written consent of the other.

(f) If either party is delayed or prevented from exercising its obligations or making deliveries in accordance with this Agreement due to circumstances beyond the reasonable control of that party including without limitation, strikes, lockouts, labor disputes, fire, explosion, act of god or other similar causes, then such failure to meet obligations or make deliveries shall not be a breach of this Agreement.

(g) Each of the provisions contained in this Agreement is distinct and severable. If one or more of the provisions of this Agreement is found to be illegal or unenforceable, this Agreement shall not be rendered inoperative or invalid but the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

(h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
(i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, licence scope).**

**What I found:**
- **Section 2 (p0028)** grants a "non-transferable and non-exclusive" licence to Sparkling *and its affiliated companies* at Authorized Locations. The affiliate limb already meets the preferred position (no notice condition required).
- **Revocability is fine:** Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid, and Section 17(c) limits termination to insolvency events and material default uncured after 30 days' notice. Section 17(c) even converts the licence to a fee-free perpetual licence if we terminate for Garman's default — a benefit to us, not flagged.
- **Where it fails the fallback:** the licence is "non-transferable", Section 3(c) prohibits assignment or transfer without Garman's written consent, and Section 20(d) (p0142) repeats the bar with **no successor/M&A carve-out**. The fallback expressly requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction, so this is a material failure, not a minor sub-element.
- **Contractors** acting on our behalf are also unaddressed, and Sections 3(e)–(f) restrict third-party use — relevant given outsourced AS400 operation.

**Redline (validated ok:true), minimal and confined to Section 2:**
1. Grant extended to "contractors acting on behalf of Sparkling or such affiliated companies."
2. New sentence overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d) permitting assignment of the Agreement and licence, without consent, to a successor in a merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, provided the successor assumes our obligations.

This reaches the preferred position while leaving the fee/Authorized Location economics and Garman's consent right for all other transfers untouched.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The grant is not revocable at Garman's discretion (Section 17(a) makes it perpetual while fees are paid, terminable only for insolvency or uncured material default under Section 17(c)(7)), and affiliates are already covered without a notice condition — so the clause is above walk-away and meets the affiliate limb of the preferred position. However, it fails the fallback on transferability: the licence is expressly "non-transferable", Section 3(c) bars assignment or transfer without Garman's written consent, and Section 20(d) repeats that bar with no carve-out for a successor in an M&A transaction. Contractors acting on our behalf are also not covered (and Section 3(f)/3(e) restrict third-party use). We therefore propose a minimal edit to Section 2 adding contractors and a successor-transfer right overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d).

Original paragraphs:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors acting on behalf of Sparkling or such affiliated companies, in each case operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Notwithstanding Sections 3(c) and 20(d), Sparkling may assign this Agreement and the licence granted under this Section 2, without Garman's consent, to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, provided such successor assumes Sparkling's obligations under this Agreement. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the grant to contractors acting on our behalf and added a successor-transfer right, since our playbook requires the licence to survive a merger or sale and to cover the third parties who operate the system for us. We are happy to keep the transfer limited to a genuine M&A successor that assumes our obligations.

input.rationale: The Agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or verification right over Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) ends at limb (g) with use covenants only and no accompanying right for Garman to audit licence compliance, count copies or access Sparkling's systems; Section 20 (General Matters) contains only time-of-essence and notice provisions, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "premises" and "remote" return no audit-type right binding us. The only examination right in the document runs in our favour (Section 16 escrow: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman"), and Section 14 confidentiality protects accounting records to which either party obtains access. With no audit right against the Customer, there is nothing exceeding the preferred position on frequency, notice, cost or system access, so the outcome is better than preferred and no redline is warranted — inviting an audit clause would create an exposure we do not currently have.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continuing for as long as the Software remains under Maintenance Services — this meets and in fact exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no additional charge under the Software Repair Service (p0077), and during the acceptance period Sparkling may reject the Software with a full refund of all amounts paid (§§ 7–8, p0057). Critically, the document contains no disclaimer of implied warranties or "AS IS" language, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and § 15 preserves recovery of direct damages. Noted but not flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording): there is no separate "professional and workmanlike manner" warranty for the installation/conversion/training services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty; the repair obligation is also framed as "best efforts" rather than an unqualified repair/replace/refund election. These are sub-elements only — the material terms (period and remedy) sit at or above the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continuing for as long as the Software remains under Maintenance Services — this meets and in fact exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no additional charge under the Software Repair Service (p0077), and during the acceptance period Sparkling may reject the Software with a full refund of all amounts paid (§§ 7–8, p0057). Critically, the document contains no disclaimer of implied warranties or "AS IS" language, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and § 15 preserves recovery of direct damages. Noted but not flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording): there is no separate "professional and workmanlike manner" warranty for the installation/conversion/training services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty; the repair obligation is also framed as "best efforts" rather than an unqualified repair/replace/refund election. These are sub-elements only — the material terms (period and remedy) sit at or above the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

reasons: Classification is correct: affiliates are already covered without a notice condition and the licence is not revocable at will (so above walk-away), but the grant is expressly 'non-transferable' and Sections 3(c)/20(d) bar assignment with no M&A successor carve-out — that is a material failure of the stated fallback ('transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction'), so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted rather than over-flagging.

Redline is directionally correct and tracks the rule's redline guidance: it inserts contractors acting on our behalf and adds a consent-free successor-transfer right expressly overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d), with a reasonable assumption-of-obligations proviso. Leaving the word 'non-transferable' in place is acceptable because the 'Notwithstanding' sentence controls.

The failed changed-character ratio on the second operation reflects the insertion of a new successor-transfer sentence, which is unavoidable given the fallback requirement; the edit otherwise preserves the original wording (AS400/Authorized Locations limits, additional-fee sentence) and is not an unnecessary rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, on-tone, correctly cites the playbook position and offers the M&A-limited fallback; it does not misstate the original clause.

Minor nit worth tightening (not disqualifying): the added 'in each case operating at Authorized Locations' now grammatically sweeps in Sparkling itself, whereas the original modifier attached to affiliated companies; consider 'and, in the case of such affiliated companies and contractors, operating at Authorized Locations' to avoid inadvertently narrowing our own use rights.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

Category: transition

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right exercisable by Garman against Sparkling:

- **Section 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the planner's most likely home for a licence-compliance audit — runs from limb (a) through limb (g) as pure use covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau) with no accompanying right for Garman to verify compliance, count copies, or access Sparkling systems.
- **Section 20 (General Matters)** contains only time-of-essence and notice mechanics.
- Text searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "premises", "remote" and "records" surface no audit-type right binding us.
- The single examination right in the document runs **in our favour**: Section 16 escrow permits Sparkling, itself or via independent experts, to examine and test the deposited materials for Garman's compliance.

Because there is no audit right against the Customer at all, there is nothing that could exceed the preferred limits on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the position is better than preferred. Consistent with the rule's direction (audits *against* Customer), the absence benefits us, so I have not proposed inserting an audit framework; doing so would manufacture an exposure we do not currently carry.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or verification right over Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) ends at limb (g) with use covenants only and no accompanying right for Garman to audit licence compliance, count copies or access Sparkling's systems; Section 20 (General Matters) contains only time-of-essence and notice provisions, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "premises" and "remote" return no audit-type right binding us. The only examination right in the document runs in our favour (Section 16 escrow: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman"), and Section 14 confidentiality protects accounting records to which either party obtains access. With no audit right against the Customer, there is nothing exceeding the preferred position on frequency, notice, cost or system access, so the outcome is better than preferred and no redline is warranted — inviting an audit clause would create an exposure we do not currently have.

p0030: Sparkling shall:
p0039: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.

Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:

Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination charge on Sparkling:

- **Section 11 (p0084)** is a bare obligation to pay Fee Schedule fees — no interest, late charge or penalty mechanic.
- **Section 17(b) (p0118)** gives us termination for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no termination fee** or residual-value payment.
- **Section 17 default provisions (p0128)** run in our favour: on Garman's default the licence converts to a perpetual, fee-free licence and Garman refunds fees for services not yet rendered.
- Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty" and interest returned nothing adverse; the sole "penalties" reference (p0090) sits inside Garman's IP indemnity of our Losses — a benefit to us, not flagged.
- Section 15 (p0105) is a mutual direct-damages-only limitation, not a stipulated-sum clause.

This satisfies the **preferred** position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees) is not needed and nothing should be raised with the counterparty under this rule.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
Sparkling shall:
(a) not copy the Software except to copy it onto another AS400 at the Authorized Locations and to make copies of the Software at each Authorized Location solely for backup purposes;
(b) not copy any of the Documentation except as required for Sparkling's internal purposes related to Sparkling's use of the Software;
(c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
(d) not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the Software;
(e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
(f) take all reasonable precautions to prevent third parties from using

the Work in any way that would constitute a breach of this Agreement including, without limitation, such precautions as Sparkling would otherwise take to protect its own proprietary software or hardware or information; and
PAGE 5
and after hours 1-306-717-1999, which is a pager number being monitored directly by qualified Garman staff.
(c) SOFTWARE REPAIR SERVICE

Should the Software not operate substantially in conformance with the Sparkling's Specifications in all material respects, Garman will use its best efforts to repair the Software under the support agreement at no additional charge to Sparkling. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Garman may charge a fee at its rates set out in the Fee Schedule to provide Software Repair Services which are required due to:
(1) failure due to Sparkling operator errors;

(2) failure to maintain Software at such updated version or release of the Software provided by Garman to Sparkling, from time to time, at no additional charge as part of the Maintenance Services or otherwise;
(3) material modification of the Software by Sparkling; or
(4) the Software being transferred to a different networking environment or hardware configuration without the prior written consent of Garman; or
(5) any failure of the hardware or the operating system not caused by Garman or the Software.
