Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: missing** (INSURANCE — Vendor insurance, severity low)

The Agreement contains no insurance provision at all — a text search for "insurance" returns zero hits, and Section 20 (General Matters) runs (a)–(i) covering time, notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractor, force majeure, severability, governing law and headings, then ends.

Insurance is expected for this vendor:
- **Section 4** — Garman installs the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location and performs conversion of Sparkling's data.
- **Section 9** — Garman personnel work on implementation alongside our project manager.

That is a vendor both attending our premises and processing our data, which is squarely the playbook's walk-away scenario when uninsured.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and Section 20 (General Matters, paragraphs (a)–(i)) ends at headings with no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement. Insurance is expected here: under Section 4 Garman installs the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location and performs conversion of Sparkling's data, and under Section 9 Garman personnel work with our project manager on implementation — i.e. a vendor that both attends our premises and processes our data, which is the playbook's walk-away scenario if uninsured. We therefore insert the preferred coverage package (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request) as a new Section 20(j), the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0134: 20. GENERAL MATTERS
p0147: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0147: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
(j) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Garman processes Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Garman shall also maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law and shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as none appears in the Agreement, because Garman installs the Software at our Authorized Locations and converts our data. Our position is CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, E&O of USD 2,000,000 and cyber liability of USD 5,000,000 where our data is processed; we can consider E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber of USD 2,000,000 if coverage limits are an issue.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment obligation on us: searches for "minimum", "commit", "purchase" and "renew" return nothing of that kind. Section 11 simply obliges us to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken, Section 2 charges additional fees only if we elect to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations, and Section 10 makes maintenance a renewable one-year term (not a multi-year committed spend). We also retain an unconditional right to terminate on ninety (90) days' notice under Section 17(b). This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only). The only usage limits on us are ordinary licence-scope restrictions in Section 3 (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), which are not volume commitments and are noted only for completeness.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment on Sparkling, which satisfies the preferred position under MINCOMMIT:

- **§11 (Fees)** — payment is limited to the fees set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken; no committed volume or spend.
- **§2 (Grant of License)** — additional fees arise only if we elect to use the Software outside the Authorized Locations, i.e. usage-based, not a commitment.
- **§10 (Maintenance and Support)** — maintenance runs "for a renewable one-year term," so there is no multi-year committed maintenance stream.
- **§17(b)** — we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice, so even the one-year maintenance period carries an exit.
- Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "purchase" and "renew" surfaced nothing resembling a take-or-pay or volume commitment.

Noted for completeness only (not deviations): §3 contains ordinary licence-scope restrictions (no copying beyond backup, no sublicensing, no reverse engineering) — these are scope terms rather than volume caps or purchase commitments, so they fall outside this rule.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment obligation on us: searches for "minimum", "commit", "purchase" and "renew" return nothing of that kind. Section 11 simply obliges us to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken, Section 2 charges additional fees only if we elect to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations, and Section 10 makes maintenance a renewable one-year term (not a multi-year committed spend). We also retain an unconditional right to terminate on ninety (90) days' notice under Section 17(b). This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only). The only usage limits on us are ordinary licence-scope restrictions in Section 3 (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), which are not volume commitments and are noted only for completeness.

p0065: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement
**Status:** All findings below verified.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement. The overall risk profile is mixed but workable: the agreement is unusually clean on several fronts that often cost us leverage, and the remaining problems are concentrated in a small number of high-value items.

What is already acceptable and requires no redline: the Vendor-side IP indemnity in Section 13 (uncapped, with procure/replace/modify remedies, and expressly excluded from the Section 15 damages limitation); the absence of any exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, liquidated-damages or audit obligation binding us; our unconditional 90-day termination-for-convenience right in Section 17(b) with no exit charge; the absence of auto-renewal (maintenance is a "renewable one-year term"); and the Section 12 warranty, which runs for the acceptance period plus one year and continues while the Software remains under Maintenance Services, with a repair remedy and a full-refund rejection right, and with no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the document.

Where we need to negotiate, there are three critical or near-critical items. First, **Section 15 contains no monetary cap at all** — direct damages are open-ended for both parties, including for us — which fails our fallback of a mutual twelve-month fee cap. Second, **Section 13 vests ownership of the entire Work in Garman, expressly including the Schedule "D" Modifications we commission and pay for**, and the agreement is silent on ownership of our data. Third, **Sections 20(d) and 3(c) impose a blanket assignment bar with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent** — walk-away territory for a customer change-of-control event, and the same defect narrows the licence grant in Section 2. Beyond those, governing law sits in the Vendor's home jurisdiction (Nova Scotia/Canada, non-exclusive venue), Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** covering all employees rather than a targeted non-solicit, and the agreement omits post-termination transition assistance and return of our data, as well as any vendor insurance covenant.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Page 6 (Section 13) | Vendor IP indemnity covering Losses, settlement and reasonable legal fees, plus procure/replace/modify remedies; not capped, as Section 15 excludes Section 13. At or above fallback. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns the whole Work including the Schedule "D" Modifications; no title passes to us; agreement silent on ownership of our data. Fails preferred and fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | Mutual exclusion of indirect damages and Section 13/14 carve-outs, but **no monetary cap whatsoever**; fails the fallback twelve-month mutual cap. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Page 10 (Section 20(d)) | Blanket mutual assignment bar, no affiliate/M&A successor carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard; reinforced one-sidedly by Section 3(c). Walk-away territory. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; licence grants are non-exclusive; Section 3 contains ordinary scope limits only. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination charge; Section 17(b) exit is fee-free. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint; Section 14 preserves an independent-development carve-out. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | Unconditional 90-day convenience right for us with no exit charge; Garman has no convenience right. Sits at fallback on the notice period. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right over us anywhere; the only examination right (Section 16 escrow) runs in our favour. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia/Canadian law, Nova Scotia courts — Vendor's home jurisdiction and outside the accepted list. Non-exclusive venue keeps it short of walk-away. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual and affiliate-covering (good), but expressly "non-transferable" with no successor carve-out and no coverage for contractors. Fails fallback on transferability. |
